feature_under_test: bounded supply-batch identity preflight for claim and result envelopes

http_h2_real_process.interpretation: the measured 0.85 percent completion-time change is too small to claim a throughput improvement

rejected_experiment.hypothesis: raising maximum consecutive supply batches per wake from 4 to 8 would remove the H3 plateau
rejected_experiment.decision: reverted because the difference is noise and the extra configuration has no demonstrated product value

rejected_claim_transaction_experiment.hypothesis: persisting all claim transitions and receipts in one 1..32 member transaction would materially reduce H2 latency
rejected_claim_transaction_experiment.decision: reverted because the difference is noise while the design holds up to 32 Work locks for the whole transaction
rejected_claim_transaction_experiment.diagnostic_conclusion: transaction begin and commit count is not the dominant claim cost; per-Attempt fence and state queries remain

remaining_bottleneck: offer creation, claim transitions, and business result acceptance still persist each Attempt in separate transactions inside every supply batch

acceptance.reason: batch preflight is safer and uses fewer database round trips, but it does not materially change sustained throughput or close the production execution gate
